title: Shape Diff Oracle: runtime compatibility checks for shadow / A/B canaries
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: When we push new model versions (canary/A-B/shadow) we frequently see subtle incompatibilities in structured outputs and function/tool-calling payloads. These manifest as missing parameters, changed types (e.g., string -> list), renamed keys, and expanded enums that downstream callers don't handle, causing silent failures or user-visible regressions. Current rollout tooling reports high-level error counts but lacks a focused compatibility oracle that (a) computes semantic diffs between declared invocation contracts and actual model outputs, (b) scores the severity, and (c) ties results to rollout actions (pause/rollback) and A/B metrics.

Goal: Build a Shape Diff Oracle service and integration in the rollout engine that validates tool-call/structured-output compatibility during shadow and A/B canaries. The oracle will produce per-request diffs, aggregate compatibility metrics, and enforce configurable gating policies for automatic rollback or manual review.
acceptance_criteria: Oracle ingests declared invocation contract for a route (OpenAPI-esque function signature or explicit JSON schema) and computes a structured diff against a model response in shadow mode
Per-request diff includes: missing required fields, extra fields, type mismatches, changed enum values, and changed parameter optionality
Aggregate compatibility score computed per-canary cohort and exposed to Console (time series + histogram)

Rollout engine supports 2 policies: (1) soft gate: flag and notify if compatibility score drops > threshold; (2) hard gate: auto-pause/rollback if severe compatibility regressions exceed configured rates
False-positive controls: configurable heuristic to ignore benign variations (null v. empty, synonyms) and threshold tuning
End-to-end test coverage: unit tests for diff logic, integration tests for shadow traffic ingestion, and an e2e canary using a synthetic model that intentionally changes schema
Documentation: Console docs and runbook describing how to interpret compatibility reports and how to adjust gating thresholds
implementation_plan: Phase 0: Spike (2d) — prototype diff engine using existing JSON Schema + custom type matcher; test against historical canary traces
Phase 1: Core service (3w) — implement high-performance comparator, per-request scoring, severity taxonomy, and small API to receive shadow responses
Phase 2: Aggregation + UI (2w) — rollup metrics, Console visualization (compatibility heatmap, per-field diff explorer), and link to request traces
Phase 3: Rollout integration (1w) — hooks into rollout controller to support soft/hard gates and auto-rollback with audit trail
Phase 4: Hardening (1w) — false positive heuristics, sampling controls, feature flags for canary/A-B/shadow scopes
rollout_strategy: Start in shadow-only mode for all existing canaries for 7 days to collect baseline compatibility metrics
Enable soft gates for a subset of low-traffic teams: notify but do not auto-pause
After tuning thresholds and heuristics, enable hard gate auto-pause for non-critical routes with explicit opt-in
A/B experiments: annotate cohorts and compute per-variant compatibility delta; block promotion when delta exceeds threshold
Provide a manual override path in Console with an audit log entry and required approver role
metrics_and_alerts: compatibility.rate.ok: percent of requests with no breaking diffs (per-route, per-model-version)
compatibility.severity.4.count: count of high-severity diffs (missing required fields) per minute
compatibility.delta.ab: difference in compatibility.rate between baseline and canary cohorts
alerts: trigger when compatibility.severity.4.count > 0.5% of sampled requests for 5m
dashboard panels: per-field change frequency, top changed keys, example request/response pairs
test_plan: Unit: combinatorial tests for type coercions and edge-cases (e.g., number-as-string)
Integration: shadow traffic pipeline feeds oracle and asserts aggregation correctness against synthetic models
E2E: staged canary where synthetic model removes a required param; verify rollout auto-pause and rollback audit entries
Chaos: fuzz inputs to ensure comparator remains performant and doesn't OOM on batched traces
decision_log: 2026-02-22 — Chose JSON Schema + lightweight heuristics as canonical comparison format instead of full protobuf delta to support heterogeneous contracts
2026-03-01 — Agreed to implement severity taxonomy with 4 levels: INFO (extras), WARN (optional field changes), ERROR (type mismatches), CRITICAL (missing required / changed semantics)
2026-03-05 — Opted to defer automatic fixes (e.g., auto-compat adapters) to a later RFC; initial scope limited to detection + gating

2026-03-07 — Luca Moreno: Prototype comparator implemented (server + in-memory cache of schemas). Performance note: avg diff time 0.8ms/request on p50 when run in bulk mode. Still optimizing p99.
2026-03-09 — Design review (Elena Park): Console wireframes approved; added a per-diff explainer panel and suggested colorblind-friendly palette for heatmap
